about: Every visible shape on the F/A-18C, region by region, with the reference photos that show it and whether the model matches (../verify/README.md, step 7). status: matches, wrong (with what is wrong), or unchecked. Numbers are the photo match's (photos.json) or the facts check's (check.py) as of the date; a shape inside the outline is only ever verified here.

2026-11-06: triangulated from 35 photos (layout.lights): the position lights' lenses under each LEX's edge aft-below the fence (19 rays over 90 deg) and at the forward tip of the fairing under each wing's fold (5 rays), the white tail light closing the right fin's upper pod (7), the strobes' red lenses on the fins' outboard faces (33), the landing light and the approach lights' stack on the nose gear's strut (8 and 10). Lenses built flush for the strobes, the LEX position lights and the tail light (their size estimated, 2 in; the tail's 1 in on the pod's end); the fold lights stand on a fairing the build does not carry and the gear lights on the provisional strut (#71): points only, the gear's at rest on the strut that carries them

the nose strips built flush in the lights material, FS 130.2-165.7 at WL 113.9, 1.7 in tall (both sides agree within 0.6 in). 2026-11-06: the others triangulated from their ends' marks (layout.strips) and built flush on the face they stand on: the fins' outboard faces FS 600.6-616.3, WL 147.5-178.1 (16-18 rays over 90 deg), and the nacelles' sides between the flap and the stabilator FS 562.1-596.8 at WL 103.8 (7-9 rays); the tip launchers' above and below the rail are points until the launchers are built (step 5). Their width is the nose strip's, not measured. The faces under them stand 1.2 in inboard (fins) and 1.5 in outboard (nacelles) of the photos' strips, within the rays' own misses

canopy.shape: aft fairing and the joint behind it
canopy.note: the fairing carries the canopy's section aft and fills out to the spine by the joint at FS 333-334, which two photos either side triangulate (layout.canopy joint): the skin's half-width there within 0.05 in. Before (2026-11-03) the spine stood up to 2 in proud of the canopy within an inch of its aft end, a 67 deg step (the user's report); the fairing now turns 11 deg an inch at most. Behind the joint (2026-11-03): the cited FS 357 section stood 2-3 in wider than the spine's side seam (layout.spine side), a bulge the user saw once the step no longer hid it; drawn through the seam's points it narrowed and let out again, a dip then hump the user saw twice more. The skin now runs from the joint to the rear fuselage on one smooth cubic per share of the section's height, within 0.74 in of the seam (dvids9820782's pair; dvids9820788 reads the joint's own foot 1.6 in inside) and with no wave (shape.wave), and the fairing's shoulders widen steadily from the canopy's section at FS 290 to the joint, as dvids7487368 shows them beside the glass's tip: swelled from the glass's pointed section within 8 in they stood a collar, and after the glass's single superellipse had narrowed them first, a notch then hump on each shoulder (user, 2026-11-04). Open: the rear fuselage's front against the seam (FS 404-430) The glass (2026-11-04): it had run down to the sill at the aft end in steps along the loft's rings (the user's report); its lower edge, read off dvids9820782 and dvids9820788 (layout.canopy glass_edge, the two within 0.5 in), rises from 3.5 in above the sill at FS 254 to WL 151.5 at FS 317, and the glass is now cut along it into a rounded tip, a broad metal panel below: every reading within 0.6 in The canopy's tail (2026-11-04, the user, three times): the old model's canopy end, a narrow bubble on a broad flat-topped base whose corner runs on aft, measured on it at the user's decision (layout.dorsal; the photos' joint and seam put the shoulder 0.6-2 in lower) and our surface built to it from 30 in ahead of the canopy's aft end to 85 in behind: within 0.3 in of its widths at 2-8 in below the top, 12-55 in aft. Its crease (2026-11-04, the user: the tail lumpy, its corner soft): the corner at the tail's foot measured on the old model every half inch (layout.dorsal crease) and laid exactly, a ring column on it and its edges shaded sharp, the tail's height the old model's from the aft end back; in place within 0.01 in and turning 85-98% of the old model's angle at five offsets, the glass ending on it over FS 295-319 where the photos' glass edge runs 0.3-0.7 in below it. The top behind the glass (2026-11-05): the canopy's top falls from the photos' last reading at FS 318 to the spine's crown at its aft end (FS 325) and the spine runs flat behind, as twelve side photos read it against the sky (layout.canopy tail); the old model's section, laid here 2026-11-04 at the user's decision, stood its hood 1.8 in higher and its base 2-2.7 in outside the head-on photos, and was taken out when the user chose the photos
